topics.titleEn: TanStack Start: A Full-Stack React Alternative
topics.angle: guide + what TanStack Start is and when to choose it over Next.js
topics.brief: Field-notes guide to TanStack Start, the team's full-stack meta-framework built on TanStack Router and Vite. Sections: how it positions against Next.js and Remix; type-safe routing and data loading; SSR and streaming; where the Vite foundation helps DX; migration and maturity caveats in 2026; when Next.js is still the safer pick. Verify: TanStack Start built on Router + Vite; full-stack positioning. Sources: TanStack docs; 2026 React trend reports (LogRocket, eSparkInfo). End with a decision checklist and a minimal starter outline.

topics.titleEn: WebGPU in 2026: GPU Power in the Browser
topics.angle: deep-dive + what WebGPU unlocks and when to reach for it in web apps
topics.brief: Story-led deep-dive on WebGPU in 2026. Sections: what WebGPU is and how it differs from WebGL; browser support status; real use cases (in-browser ML inference, data viz, image/video processing, games); a minimal compute-shader example concept; performance wins and the fallback story for unsupported browsers; when it is overkill. Verify: WebGPU support across major browsers in 2026; on-device inference use case. Sources: MDN WebGPU docs; browser status pages. End with a should-you-use-WebGPU checklist and gotchas.

topics.titleEn: Wiring AI Agents Into Your CI/CD Safely
topics.angle: guide + run coding agents in pipelines with guardrails that prevent runaway changes
topics.brief: Contrarian guide to putting AI coding agents inside CI/CD without letting them run wild. Sections: good jobs for agents (triage, dependency bumps, test generation, first-pass fixes) versus jobs to keep human; sandboxing, least-privilege tokens and no prod write access; requiring human approval and signed commits; cost and rate controls; auditing agent actions and rollback. Verify: 2026 trend of agent guardrails and least-privilege for autonomous tools. Sources: CI/CD and agent-safety guidance; vendor docs. End with a pipeline-integration checklist and a red-lines list.

topics.titleEn: Preview Environments for Every Pull Request
topics.angle: how-to + spin up ephemeral per-PR environments so reviewers test real changes
topics.brief: Field-notes guide to ephemeral preview environments per pull request. Sections: why per-PR environments cut review friction and catch bugs early; approaches (platform-native previews, Kubernetes namespaces, docker-compose on demand); seeding data and stubbing external services; secrets and cost controls; tearing down automatically to avoid sprawl; database branching to isolate schema changes. Verify: preview envs reduce 'works on my machine' and speed review. Sources: platform docs (Vercel/Netlify), GitOps guides. End with a build-vs-buy decision list and a teardown checklist.

topics.titleTr: Bilgi Calisanlari Icin Gunluk AI Is Akislari
topics.titleEn: Daily AI Workflows for Knowledge Workers
topics.angle: how-to + practical daily routines that put ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini to real work
topics.brief: Story-led playbook of daily AI routines for knowledge workers. Sections: inbox and meeting triage; turning notes into drafts and decisions (ChatGPT Work / Claude); research and summarizing with citations you verify; Gemini inside Workspace for docs and sheets; scheduled/recurring tasks; guardrails against over-trusting output and leaking sensitive data. Verify: ChatGPT Work and agent/scheduled-task capabilities; Gemini-in-Workspace features in 2026. Sources: vendor guides; productivity write-ups. End with a copy-and-adapt daily template and a 'never delegate this' list.

topics.titleTr: AI ile Kod Incelemesi: Guven Ama Dogrula
topics.titleEn: AI Code Review: Trust, but Verify
topics.angle: mistakes + use AI code reviewers well and know exactly what they miss
topics.brief: Contrarian guide to AI code review as a complement, not a replacement, for human review. Sections: what AI reviewers catch reliably (style, obvious bugs, boilerplate risks) versus what they miss (intent, architecture, security context, subtle concurrency); false-positive fatigue and how to tune it; keeping humans on design and security-critical paths; integrating AI review in the pipeline without rubber-stamping. Verify: 2026 reality that a large share of code is AI-generated, raising review stakes. Sources: 2026 AI-coding trend reports; review best-practice guides. End with an AI-plus-human review checklist. Distinct from general code-review process posts.
